metas.name: Agave salmiana
metas.note: Agave salmiana, also known as pulque agaves, have wide, smooth, curling leaves, and a crown-like appearance. They are common in the central Mexican valley and further north around the city of San Luis Potosi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Agave tequilana
metas.note: Vast fields of blue agave (Agave tequilana), used to produce tequila, are mostly found in Jalisco and Nayarit.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Asymmetric mushroom-like insulator pole
metas.note: Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Black tar
metas.note:
Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line can be seen in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.

NOTE: This is most reliable when the tar is not faded.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Blindingly white soil
metas.note:
Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.

NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Blue Myrtle Cacti
metas.note: The Blue Myrtle Cacti have short arms that uniformly curve and point upwards. It is abundantly found in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Boojum trees
metas.note: Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Brittlebush
metas.note: Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Chihuahua cross
metas.note: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Coahuila gold tufts
metas.note: These gold tufts of grass in a line right next to the road are most commonly found in Coahuila.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Cobblestone pavement
metas.note: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Concrete hanging insulator pole
metas.note: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Giant Cardon
metas.note: The Mexican Giant Cardon is an extremely common cacti in the Baja California peninsula. It can be identified through its large sprawling arms stemming from a singular trunk and ribbed exterior.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Grainy pavement
metas.note:
Grainy pavement with a blue-ish grey tinge is a common sight for the states of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.

NOTE: In Tamaulipas, larger roads very commonly feature dashed outer lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Guanajuato extremely dark fields
metas.note: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Hexagonal tiles pavement
metas.note: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Jalisco bollards
metas.note: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text ‘Jalisco’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Light coloured rock walls
metas.note:
These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.

Comment from Vincent: When not in the sun, the rock walls appear darker, but it's likely the same type of rock.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mesh body pole
metas.note: Poles with a mesh body are most commonly found in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Nayarit bollard
metas.note: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Oaxaca pavement
metas.note: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Oil palm plantations
metas.note: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Red agricultural fields
metas.note: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Saguaro Cacti
metas.note: The Saguaro Cacti can be spotted in the western half of Sonora, featuring short curving arms that stem from a main trunk.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Western, shorter pine forest
metas.note: The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: White middle roadlines
metas.note: White middle roadlines are most commonly found in Tabasco.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Wooden hanging insulator pole
metas.note: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Yucca filifera
metas.note: Yucca filifera, also known as tree yucca, as well as yucca decipiens are most commonly seen in San Luis Potosi and Zacatecas as well as some of the bordering northern states. They can be recognised by their oblong rosettes of sharp green leaves branching from a single trunk, similar to a tree.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.
